{1} Al-Anfal (the spoils of war) are the booty which Allah grants to this Ummah from the wealth of the disbelievers. These verses in this surah were revealed concerning the events of Badr, the first great spoil that the Muslims seized from the polytheists, and a dispute arose among some of the Muslims over it. So they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about it, and Allah revealed: ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾: how are they to be divided, and to whom are they to be distributed? ﴿Say﴾: the spoils belong to Allah and His Messenger, who dispose of them wherever they wish. So you have no objection to the ruling of Allah and His Messenger. Rather, when Allah and His Messenger have ruled, it is incumbent upon you to accept their judgment and submit the matter to them. This is included in His words: ﴿so fear Allah﴾ by complying with His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, ﴿and set right what is between you﴾; that is, reconcile what lies between you of enmity, estrangement and aversion, through mutual affection, love and kinship. By this, your word will be united and what arises from estrangement, such as quarrelling, contention and dispute, will be removed.

Included in setting right what lies between people is improving one's character toward them and pardoning those among them who do wrong, for by this much of the hatred and aversion that lies in the hearts is removed. The comprehensive matter encompassing all of this is His words: ﴿and obey Allah and His Messenger, if you are believers﴾. Indeed, faith calls to obedience to Allah and His Messenger, just as whoever does not obey Allah and His Messenger is not a believer, and whoever's obedience to Allah and His Messenger is deficient, that is due to the deficiency of his faith.

{2} Since faith is of two kinds: complete faith, which entails praise, commendation and complete success; and faith short of that, He mentioned complete faith, saying: ﴿The believers are only those﴾: the definite article here is for totality, encompassing all the branches of faith, ﴿who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble﴾; that is, they fear and are awed, and the fear of Allah's exalted majesty obliges them to refrain from the prohibited things, for the greatest sign of the fear of Allah is that it restrains its possessor from sins. ﴿And when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith﴾: the reason for this is that they give ear to it and direct their hearts to contemplating it; at that point their faith increases, because reflection is one of the deeds of the heart, and because it necessarily clarifies for them a meaning they were ignorant of, and reminds them of what they had forgotten, or produces in their hearts a desire for good and a longing for the honour of their Lord, or a trembling from punishments and a restraint from sins. All of this is what faith increases by. ﴿And upon their Lord﴾ alone, with no partner, ﴿they rely﴾; that is, they depend in their hearts upon their Lord to bring about their benefits and to ward off their harms, both religious and worldly, and they trust that Allah, exalted is He, will do that. Reliance (tawakkul) is what carries all deeds; they neither come into existence nor are they perfected except through it.

{3} ﴿Who establish the prayer﴾: obligatory and voluntary, with its outward and inward acts, such as presence of heart in it, which is the spirit and essence of prayer. ﴿And from what We have provided them they spend﴾: obligatory expenditures, such as zakat, expiations, and maintenance of wives, relatives and those whom their right hands possess, and recommended expenditures, such as charity in every avenue of good.

{4} ﴿Those﴾: who have attained those attributes, ﴿are the believers in truth﴾: because they have combined Islam and faith, inward deeds and outward deeds, knowledge and action, and fulfilling the rights of Allah and the rights of His servants.

Almighty Allah placed the deeds of the heart first, because they are the root of the deeds of the limbs and superior to them. In this is evidence that faith increases and decreases: it increases by performing obedience and decreases by its opposite. It is also incumbent upon the servant to safeguard his faith and nurture it, and the most important means of achieving that is reflecting upon the Book of Allah and contemplating its meanings. Then He mentioned the reward of the believers in truth, saying: ﴿For them are ranks with their Lord﴾; that is, elevated ranks according to the loftiness of their deeds. ﴿And forgiveness﴾ for their sins, ﴿and a noble provision﴾: which is what Allah has prepared for them in the abode of His honour, that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. This indicates that whoever does not reach their level in faith, even if he enters Paradise, will not attain what they attained of the complete honour of Allah.

Almighty Allah placed before this great, blessed battle the attributes which the believers must uphold, because whoever upholds them, his circumstances become upright and his deeds become sound, the greatest of which is striving in His way.

{5–6} Just as their faith is true faith and their reward is the truth that God promised them, so too did God bring His Messenger (ﷺ) out of his house to meet the polytheists at Badr with the truth that God loves and has decreed and ordained. Although the believers had not thought, when they set out, that there would be fighting between them and their enemy, once it became clear to them that this was happening, a group of the believers began to argue with the Prophet (ﷺ) about it and to dislike meeting their enemy, as if they were being driven to death while they looked on! Likewise, those whom God rebuked complied with the jihad most fully, and God made them firm and provided for them the means by which their hearts would be reassured, as will be mentioned below.

{7} The origin of their going forth was that they intended to intercept a caravan that Quraysh had sent with Abu Sufyan ibn Harb to al-Sham, a large caravan. When they heard that it was returning from al-Sham, the Prophet (ﷺ) called the people to go out, and there went with him three hundred and some-odd men, with seventy camels which they rode in turns and on which they carried their goods. Quraysh heard news of them and went out to prevent their caravan, with a large number and abundant equipment of weapons, horses and men, their number reaching nearly a thousand. God promised the believers one of the two groups: either they would gain victory over the caravan, or over the armed host. They loved the caravan because the Muslims were lacking in wealth and because it was unarmed (lit. "not possessing might"). But God loved for them, and willed, something higher than what they loved: He willed that they should gain victory over the host in which the great nobles and champions of the polytheists had gone out. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 8, verses 9–14:

{9} That is: remember the blessing of Allah upon you when your meeting with your enemy drew near; you called for help from your Lord and asked Him to aid and support you. {So He answered you}: and He relieved you through several matters, among them: Allah reinforced you {with a thousand of the angels, following one another}; that is, some of them follow others.

{10} {And Allah did not make it}; that is, the sending down of the angels, {except as good news}; that is, so that your souls might be gladdened by it, {and that your hearts might be reassured thereby}. Otherwise, victory is in the hand of Allah, not by multitude of numbers or abundance of equipment. {Indeed, Allah is Almighty}: none can overcome Him, rather He is the Subduer who forsakes those who have reached whatever heights of numbers, strength of troops and weaponry they have reached, {All-Wise}: in that He decreed matters by their causes and placed things in their proper places.

{11} And from His victory and His answering your supplication: He sent down upon you a slumber {overcoming you}; that is, it removes from your hearts the fear and dread, and it becomes {security} for you and a sign of victory and tranquility. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 8, verses 15–16:

{15} Allah, exalted is He, commands His believing servants to have faith-born courage, to be strong in carrying out His command, and to strive to obtain the means that strengthen hearts and bodies, and He forbids them from fleeing when the two armies meet. He says: {O you who have believed, when you meet those who disbelieve advancing [in battle]} — that is, in the battle line, when the men press upon one another and draw close to each other — {then do not turn your backs to them} — rather, stand firm against them and be patient in facing their blows. For in that is support for the religion of Allah, strength for the hearts of the believers, and terror struck into the disbelievers.

{16} {And whoever turns his back to them on such a day, except one who swerves [for a tactical purpose] or one who withdraws to join another company, has certainly drawn upon himself anger from Allah, and his refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination} — that is, he returns {with anger from Allah}; his abode, that is, his dwelling place, is {Hell, and wretched is the destination}.

This indicates that fleeing from the battle line without an excuse is among the greatest of the major sins, as the authentic hadiths have reported, and as this verse explicitly states with this severe threat. The implication of the verse is that one who swerves for the sake of fighting — that is, one who shifts from one side to another so that he is better placed for fighting and more effective against his enemy — there is no harm in that, because he has not turned his back in flight; rather, he turned his back in order to gain the higher ground over his enemy, or to come at him from a place where he can catch him unaware, or to deceive him by that, or for other purposes of those who wage war. And one who withdraws to a company that protects him and helps him fight the disbelievers — this is permissible. If the company is within the army, the matter in this is clear. If the company is outside the place of the battle, such as the defeat of the Muslims before the disbelievers and their taking refuge in a city of the Muslim lands or in another army of the Muslims, then there are reports from the Companions indicating that this is permissible. Perhaps this is restricted to when the Muslims think that retreat is the better outcome and preserves them; but if they think that by standing firm in fighting the disbelievers they will overcome them, then it is far-fetched that this would be among the situations in which retreat is permitted, since on this view the forbidden flight would not arise. This verse is unrestricted, and its restriction by number will come at the end of the surah.

{17} God, exalted is He, says, when the polytheists were routed on the Day of Badr and the Muslims killed them: ﴿So you did not kill them﴾: by your own strength and power; ﴿but it was God who killed them﴾: since He helped you in that by what has been mentioned before; ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but it was God who threw﴾. {18} ﴿That﴾: the victory from God for you, ﴿and that God weakens the plot of the disbelievers﴾; that is, He makes weak every scheme and plot by which they plot against Islam and its people, and makes their scheming recoil upon them.

{19} ﴿If you seek a decision﴾: O polytheists; that is, you ask God to bring down His might and punishment upon the aggressors and wrongdoers. ﴿Then the decision has come to you﴾: when God brought upon you from His punishment what was a deterrent to you and a lesson for the God-fearing. ﴿And if you desist﴾: from seeking a decision, ﴿it is better for you﴾: because perhaps He would have granted you respite and the retribution would not have been hastened upon you. ﴿And if you return﴾: to seeking a decision and fighting the party of God, the believers, ﴿We will return﴾: in giving them victory over you, ﴿and your company will avail you nothing﴾; that is, your helpers and supporters upon whom you rely and with whom you fight, anything. ﴿And that God is with the believers﴾: and whoever God is with is the one who is victorious, even if he is weak and few in number.

Otherwise, if they were to do what God commanded in every respect, no banner of theirs would be routed with a lasting rout, and their enemy would never prevail over them.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 8, verse 24–25:

{24} Allah commands His believing servants with what faith requires of them, which is to respond to Allah and to the Messenger; that is, to submit to what they have commanded, to hasten to it, and to call others to it, and to avoid what they have forbidden, to refrain from it, and to forbid it. His saying: ﴿when He calls you to that which gives you life﴾ is a description that accompanies everything to which Allah and His Messenger call, and an explanation of its benefit and wisdom; for the life of the heart and the spirit lies in worshipping Allah Most High and in constantly adhering to obedience to Him and to obedience to His Messenger. Then He warned against not responding to Allah and to the Messenger, saying: ﴿And know that Allah comes between a man and his heart﴾: so beware of rejecting the command of Allah the first time it reaches you, lest it be made impossible for you to obey it when you later want to, and your hearts become divided; for Allah comes between a man and his heart, turning hearts as He wills and directing them as He pleases. Therefore let the servant often say: "O Turner of the hearts, keep my heart firm upon Your religion. O Director of the hearts, turn my heart to Your obedience." ﴿And that to Him you will be gathered﴾; that is, you will be assembled for a Day about which there is no doubt, when He will recompense the doer of good for his good and the doer of evil for his disobedience.

{25} ﴿And beware of a trial which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively﴾: rather, it will strike the perpetrator of wrong and others as well. This happens when wrongdoing becomes apparent and is not changed, for its punishment encompasses the perpetrator and others. This trial is intensified by neglecting to forbid evil and by failing to suppress the people of evil and corruption, and by not allowing them to commit sins and wrongdoing as far as it is possible. ﴿And know that Allah is severe in punishment﴾: for whoever exposes himself to His displeasure and turns away from His pleasure.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 8, verse 29:

{29} The servant's compliance with the taqwa (God-consciousness, fear of God) of his Lord is the emblem of happiness and the sign of success. God has ordained many goods of this world and the Hereafter as consequences of taqwa. Here He mentions that whoever fears God obtains four things, each of which is better than this world and everything in it:

The first: al-Furqan (the criterion that distinguishes truth from falsehood), which is the knowledge and guidance by which its possessor distinguishes between guidance and misguidance, truth and falsehood, the lawful and the unlawful, and the people of happiness from the people of wretchedness.

The second and third: takfir al-sayyi'at (the expiation of misdeeds) and maghfirat al-dhunub (the forgiveness of sins). Each of these is included in the other when mentioned alone, but when they are mentioned together, takfir al-sayyi'at is interpreted as the expiation of minor sins, and maghfirat al-dhunub as the expiation of major sins.

The fourth: the great reward and the abundant recompense for whoever fears Him and prefers His pleasure over the desires of his own soul.

{And God is the Possessor of great bounty.}

{30} That is: {And} remember, O Messenger, the blessing Allah bestowed upon you, {when those who disbelieved plotted against you}: when the polytheists consulted together in the House of Assembly (Dar al-Nadwa) about what to do with the Prophet ﷺ. They considered three options: either to confine him by imprisoning and binding him, or to kill him and thereby, in their own estimation, be rid of his evil, or to expel him and drive him out of their lands. Each of them put forward an opinion he held, but their view came to agree on an opinion proposed by their wickedest man, Abu Jahl, may Allah curse him, namely that they should take one young man from each of the tribes of Quraysh, give each of them a sharp sword, and that they should all strike him together as one man, so that his blood would be spread among the tribes, and the Banu Hashim would then accept the blood-money, and they would be unable to resist all of Quraysh. So they lay in wait for the Prophet ﷺ at night, to strike him when he rose from his bed. But revelation came to him from heaven, and he went out before them, threw dust upon their heads and departed. Allah blinded their eyes to him, until, when they grew impatient for him, someone came to them and said: "May Allah frustrate you! Muhammad has gone out and thrown dust upon your heads!" Each of them shook the dust from his head. Allah protected His Messenger from them and permitted him to emigrate to Medina, and he emigrated there. Allah strengthened him with his Companions, the Emigrants (Muhajirun) and the Helpers (Ansar). His affair continued to rise until he entered Mecca by force and subdued its people, who submitted to him and came under his rule, after he had left it secretly, fearful for his own life. Glory be to the Subtle One with His servant, whom none can overcome. And his saying:

{31} Exalted is He, stating the obstinacy of those who denied the Messenger (ﷺ): {And when Our verses are recited to them}: which indicate the truth of what the Messenger brought, {they say, "We have heard. If we wished, we could say the like of this. This is nothing but the myths of the ancients."}: This is from their obstinacy and their wrongdoing. Otherwise, Allah had already challenged them to produce a surah like it, and to call upon whomever they could besides Allah, but they were unable to do so, and their incapacity became clear. So this statement uttered by this speaker is a mere claim that reality itself has refuted. He (ﷺ) was known to be unlettered; he could neither read nor write, and he did not travel to study the reports of the ancients. Yet he brought this glorious Book, "falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it; it is a revelation from One Wise, Praiseworthy."

{32} {And when they said, "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment."}: They said this with certainty in their falsehood and ignorance of what ought to be said in such a plea. For if, when they stood upon their falsehood with its doubts and deceptions, which did not give them any insight or certainty about it, they had said to the one who debated them and claimed that the truth was with him: "If this is the truth from you, then guide us to it," it would have been better for them and more concealing of their wrongdoing. But since they said, {"O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You..."} to the end of the verse, it became known from this statement alone that they are the foolish, the dull, the ignorant, and the wrongdoers.

Although they uttered this statement openly before the assembled people, they knew its ugliness, and so they feared its consequences falling upon them, and they would seek Allah's forgiveness. Therefore He said: {Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness}: This is a barrier that prevents punishment from befalling them after its causes had been established.

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 8, verses 45–49:**

{45} He, the Exalted, says: ﴿O you who have believed, when you encounter a company [of disbelievers fighting you]﴾; that is, a group of the disbelievers who fight you. ﴿Then stand firm﴾ for fighting them, and employ patience and restraint of the self in this great act of obedience, whose outcome is honour and victory. Seek help in this by increasing your remembrance of Allah. ﴿That you may succeed﴾; that is, that you may attain what you seek of triumph over your enemies. Patience, steadfastness, and frequent remembrance of Allah are among the greatest causes of victory.

{46} ﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger﴾ in carrying out what they have commanded and following it in all circumstances. ﴿And do not dispute﴾ in a manner that causes the hearts to scatter and separate, ﴿lest you lose courage﴾; that is, lest you become cowardly, ﴿and your strength depart﴾; that is, your resolve dissolves, your power is dispersed, and the victory promised to you for obedience to Allah and His Messenger is lifted from you. ﴿And be patient﴾ by restraining your souls in obedience to Allah. ﴿Indeed, Allah is with the patient﴾ through help, victory, and support.

{47} ﴿And be humble before your Lord and submit to Him, and do not be like those who went out from their homes insolently and to be seen by people and who averted [others] from the way of Allah﴾; that is, this was their aim in going out, and this is what brought them forth from their homes: seeking arrogance and insolence on earth, and so that people would see them and boast before them. The greatest purpose was that they went out to bar from the path of Allah whoever wished to follow it. ﴿And Allah is encompassing of what they do﴾. Therefore He has informed you of their intentions and warned you not to resemble them, for He will surely punish them with the most severe punishment for that. So let your purpose in going out be the Face of Allah, the elevation of the religion of Allah, the prevention of [people] from the paths that lead to the wrath and punishment of Allah, and the drawing of people to the straight path of Allah that leads to the Gardens of Bliss.

{48} ﴿And [mention] when Satan made their deeds appear pleasing to them﴾; he made them seem good in their hearts [and deceived them], ﴿and said, "No one among the people can overcome you today, and indeed I am your protector"﴾; for you are in a number, equipment, and condition in which Muhammad and those with him cannot match you. ﴿And indeed, I am a protector for you﴾ from anyone who might come upon you and whose harm you fear. This is because Iblis had appeared to the Quraysh in the form of Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum al-Mudlaji, and they had feared the Banu Mudlij because of an enmity that existed between them. So Satan said to them, "I am your protector!" Their souls were reassured, and they set out confidently and determined. But when ﴿the two armies sighted each other﴾, the Muslims and the disbelievers, Satan saw Jibril (peace be upon him) restraining the angels, and he was struck with intense fear. ﴿He turned back on his heels﴾; that is, he fled in retreat. ﴿And he said﴾ to those whom he had deceived and deluded: ﴿"Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I see what you do not see"﴾; that is, I see the angels, against whom no one has the power to fight. ﴿"Indeed, I fear Allah"﴾; that is, I fear that He will hasten punishment upon me in this world. ﴿And Allah is severe in punishment.﴾

It is also possible that Satan had embellished [the matter] for them and whispered into their breasts that no one among the people could overcome them that day and that he was their protector. Then, when he had brought them to their watering place, he withdrew from them and disowned them, as Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Like the example of Satan when he says to man, "Disbelieve." But when he disbelieves, [Satan] says, "Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds." So it was that the end of both of them was that they were in the Fire, abiding eternally therein. And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.﴾

{49} ﴿When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease﴾ say; that is, doubt and suspicion among the weak in faith, regarding the believers when they advanced, despite their small number, to fight the polytheists, despite their great number: ﴿"Their religion has deluded these"﴾; that is, the religion they follow has led them into these situations for which they have neither power nor capacity. They say this out of contempt for them and to belittle their intellects. By Allah, they themselves are the ones lacking in intellect and weak in judgment. Faith compels its possessor to advance upon great matters that vast armies would not undertake. The believer who relies upon Allah knows that there is no power, no strength, and no ability for anyone except through Allah, the Exalted; that if all creation gathered to benefit a person by the weight of an atom, they could not benefit him; and if they gathered to harm him, they could not harm him except with something Allah has decreed for him. He knows that he is upon the truth and that Allah, the Exalted, is Wise and Merciful in all that He decrees and ordains. Therefore he does not care about what he advances upon, whether of strength or multitude. He is confident in his Lord, his heart is at peace, neither fearful nor cowardly. For this reason He says: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then indeed, Allah is Almighty﴾; no strength overcomes His might. ﴿Wise﴾ in what He decrees and carries out.

For this reason He said: {So if you gain dominance over them in war}; that is, you find them in a state of warfare in which they have no covenant or pact. {Then disperse, by means of them, those behind them}; that is, make an example of them to others, and inflict upon them such punishment that they become a lesson for those after them, {that they may take heed}; that is, those behind them [may] refrain from their conduct, so that they do not suffer what they suffered. This is among the benefits of punishments and prescribed penalties for sins: they are a cause for the restraint of those who have not committed sins, and a deterrent for those who have committed them, so that they do not return to them. The restriction of this punishment to war indicates that the disbeliever, even if he is greatly treacherous and quick to betray, is not permitted to be betrayed or punished once he has been given a covenant.

{58} That is: if there is between you and a people a covenant and a pact to refrain from fighting, and you fear treachery from them, meaning that there has appeared from the indications of their circumstances what points to their treachery, without their having explicitly declared treachery. {Then throw back to them}: their covenant; that is, cast it back at them, and inform them that there is no covenant between you and them, {on equal terms}; that is, so that your knowledge and their knowledge of this become equal. The verse indicates that if actual [certain] treachery is found from them, you do not need to throw back their covenant to them, because you were not fearing it from them; rather, it was known, and because there is no benefit in it, and because of His words: {on equal terms}, and here your betrayal was already known to all. Its implication also indicates that if you do not fear treachery from them, in that no indication of it has appeared from them, then it is not permissible to throw back the covenant to them; rather, it is obligatory to fulfill [it] until its term is completed.

{59} That is: Let not those who disbelieve in their Lord and deny His signs think that they have outstripped God or escaped Him, for they cannot overpower Him, and God is ever watchful over them (lahum bil-mirsad). He, the Exalted, has perfect wisdom in granting them respite and not hastening their punishment, of which one part is the testing and trial of His believing servants, and their provision for themselves from obedience to Him and from what pleases Him, by which they reach lofty ranks and attain to characteristics and qualities which they could not have reached otherwise. Therefore He said to His believing servants:

{60} That is: {Prepare against them}, against your enemies, the disbelievers who strive to destroy you and nullify your religion, {whatever you can of strength}; that is, everything you are able to muster of mental and physical strength, of weapons of every kind, and of whatever else helps in fighting them. This includes the crafts by which all kinds of weapons and equipment are made: cannons, machine guns, rifles, aircraft, land and naval vessels, [fortresses,] castles and trenches, means of defence, and the sound judgment and statecraft by which the Muslims advance and by which the evil of their enemies is repelled. This reason exists in that time, namely striking terror into the enemies, and the ruling revolves around its cause. Among the greatest things that help in fighting them is spending wealth in jihad against the disbelievers. For this reason the Exalted said, encouraging this: {And whatever you spend in the way of Allah}, whether little or much, {will be repaid to you}: its reward on the Day of Resurrection multiplied many times over, so that spending in the way of Allah is multiplied to seven hundred times and to many more times. {And you will not be wronged}; that is, nothing of its reward and recompense will be diminished from you.

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 8, verses 61–64:**

{61} God Most High says: ﴿And if they incline to peace﴾, meaning: the disbelieving combatants. That is, if they incline to *al-salm* (peace), which is reconciliation and the cessation of fighting, ﴿then incline to it, and put your trust in God﴾, meaning: grant them what they ask, relying upon your Lord. For in this there are many benefits. Among them: seeking well-being is desirable at all times, so if they are the ones who initiate it, granting their request is all the more fitting.

Among them also: in it is a rest for your strength and a preparation on your part for fighting them at another time, should that be needed. Among them: when you make peace and some of you are secure from others, and each is able to know what the other holds to, then Islam will rise and not be risen above. Everyone who has intellect and insight, if he has fairness, will necessarily prefer it over other religions, because of its goodness in its commands and prohibitions, its goodness in its dealings with creation, and its justice toward them. There is no tyranny in it and no oppression in any way. Then those who desire it and follow it will increase, and this peace becomes a help to the Muslims against the disbelievers.

{62–63} Nothing is feared from peace except one matter: that the disbelievers intend by it to deceive the Muslims and seize an opportunity against them. So God informed them that He is sufficient for them and will suffice against their deception, and that its harm will return upon them. He said: ﴿And if they intend to deceive you, then God is sufficient for you﴾, meaning: He suffices you against what would harm you, and He is the one who manages your affairs and concerns. For you have already received from His sufficiency and His support what settles your heart. ﴿It is He who supported you with His help and with the believers﴾, meaning: He aided you with a heavenly aid, which is the victory from Him that nothing can withstand, and aided you through the believers, by destining them to support you. ﴿And He joined their hearts﴾: so they gathered, became harmonious, and their strength increased through their unity. This was not by the effort of anyone, nor by any power other than the power of God. ﴿If you had spent everything on the earth entirely﴾, of gold, silver, and other things, to unite them after that great aversion and division, ﴿you could not have joined their hearts﴾, because none can turn hearts except God Most High. ﴿But God joined them; indeed He is Mighty and Wise﴾. Among His might is that He joined their hearts and gathered them after division, as He said Most High: ﴿And remember God's favor upon you, when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together, so that by His favor you became brothers. And you were on the brink of a pit of Fire, and He saved you from it﴾.

{64} Then God Most High said: ﴿O Prophet, God is sufficient for you﴾, meaning: He suffices you, ﴿and for those of the believers who follow you﴾, meaning: and He suffices your followers among the believers. This is a promise from God to His believing servants who follow His Messenger, of sufficiency and victory over their enemies. When they bring about the cause, which is faith and following, then He will necessarily suffice them in what concerns them of the affairs of religion and of the world. The sufficiency is only withheld when its condition is absent.

{65} God says to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿O Prophet, urge the believers to fight﴾; that is, rouse them and spur them to it with everything that strengthens their resolve and energizes their aspirations: by encouraging jihad and confronting the enemies, and by warning against the opposite; by mentioning the virtues of courage and patience and what follows from them of good in this world and the Hereafter; and by mentioning the harms of cowardice, that it is one of the base characteristics that diminish both religion and manliness; and that courage is more fitting for the believers than for others. ﴿If you endure, they [too] endure as you endure, and you hope from God for what they do not hope for﴾. ﴿If there are among you twenty steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are among you a hundred, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve﴾: one of you equals ten of the disbelievers. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 8, verses 67–69:

{67} This is a reproach from God to His Messenger and the believers on the day of Badr, when they took the polytheists captive and spared them for the sake of ransom. The opinion of the Commander of the Faithful, ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, in this situation was to kill them and wipe them out. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿It is not for a Prophet to have captives until he inflicts a massacre upon the land.﴾ That is: it is not fitting or proper for him, when fighting the disbelievers who want to extinguish the light of God and strive to quench His religion, and that no one on the face of the earth should worship God, that he hastens to take them captive and spare them for the sake of the ransom that comes from them. That is a small, passing benefit compared to the greater interest that calls for their annihilation and the ending of their evil. So as long as they have evil and power, it is more proper that they not be taken captive. But once they have been thoroughly subdued, their evil has been nullified, and their affair has been crushed, then there is no harm in taking captives from them and sparing them. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿You desire﴾, by taking the ransom and sparing them, ﴿the goods of this worldly life﴾; that is, not for a benefit that returns to your religion. ﴿But God desires the Hereafter﴾, by exalting His religion, granting victory to His allies, and making their word higher than others, so He commands you with what leads to that. ﴿And God is Mighty and Wise.﴾ That is: perfect in might. Had He willed to grant victory over the disbelievers without fighting, He would have done so, but He is Wise, testing some of you by means of others.

{68} ﴿Had it not been for a decree from God that preceded﴾, by which the divine decree and destiny were determined, that He had made the spoils lawful for you, and that God had lifted from you, O Ummah, the punishment, ﴿a great punishment would have touched you for what you took.﴾ And in a hadith: "Had a punishment descended on the day of Badr, none would have been saved from it except ʿUmar."

{69} ﴿So eat of what you have taken as lawful and good.﴾ This is among His kindness, exalted is He, toward this Ummah, that He made the spoils lawful for it, and they were not made lawful for any nation before it. ﴿And fear God﴾, in all your affairs, and persist in it as thanks for God's blessings upon you. ﴿Indeed, God is Forgiving﴾, forgiving all sins for whoever repents to Him, and forgiving all disobedience for whoever has not associated anything with Him, ﴿Merciful﴾, toward you, in that He permitted you the spoils and made them lawful and good.

God, the Exalted, said: ﴿It is not for a Prophet to have captives until he inflicts a massacre upon the land.﴾ That is: it is not fitting or proper for him, when fighting the disbelievers who want to extinguish the light of God and strive to quench His religion, and that no one on the face of the earth should worship God, that he hastens to take them captive and spare them for the sake of the ransom that comes from them. That is a small, passing benefit compared to the greater interest that calls for their annihilation and the ending of their evil. So as long as they have evil and power, it is more proper that they not be taken captive. But once they have been thoroughly subdued, their evil has been nullified, and their affair has been crushed, then there is no harm in taking captives from them and sparing them. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿You desire﴾, by taking the ransom and sparing them, ﴿the goods of this worldly life﴾; that is, not for a benefit that returns to your religion. ﴿But God desires the Hereafter﴾, by exalting His religion, granting victory to His allies, and making their word higher than others, so He commands you with what leads to that. ﴿And God is Mighty and Wise.﴾ That is: perfect in might. Had He willed to grant victory over the disbelievers without fighting, He would have done so, but He is Wise, testing some of you by means of others.

{68} ﴿Had it not been for a decree from God that preceded﴾, by which the divine decree and destiny were determined, that He had made the spoils lawful for you, and that God had lifted from you, O Ummah, the punishment, ﴿a great punishment would have touched you for what you took.﴾ And in a hadith: "Had a punishment descended on the day of Badr, none would have been saved from it except ʿUmar."

{69} ﴿So eat of what you have taken as lawful and good.﴾ This is among His kindness, exalted is He, toward this Ummah, that He made the spoils lawful for it, and they were not made lawful for any nation before it. ﴿And fear God﴾, in all your affairs, and persist in it as thanks for God's blessings upon you. ﴿Indeed, God is Forgiving﴾, forgiving all sins for whoever repents to Him, and forgiving all disobedience for whoever has not associated anything with Him, ﴿Merciful﴾, toward you, in that He permitted you the spoils and made them lawful and good.

{70} This was revealed concerning the captives of the day of Badr, among whom was al-'Abbas, the paternal uncle of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When ransom was demanded from him, he claimed that he had been a Muslim before that, but they did not waive the ransom from him. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed, as a consolation to his heart and to those who were in his situation: ﴿O Prophet, say to those captives in your hands: If Allah knows any good in your hearts, He will give you better than what has been taken from you﴾; that is, of wealth, by facilitating for you from His bounty much good more than what was taken from you. ﴿And He will forgive you﴾: your sins, and admit you into Paradise. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. Allah fulfilled His promise to al-'Abbas and others, so that after that he acquired a great deal of wealth. Once, when a large amount of wealth came to the Prophet (ﷺ), al-'Abbas came to him, and he (ﷺ) instructed him to take from it with his garment whatever he could carry, so he took from it what he nearly could not lift.

{71} ﴿And if they intend to betray you﴾: in seeking to fight you and break with you, ﴿then they have betrayed Allah before, so He gave (you) power over them﴾: so let them beware of betraying you, for He, the Exalted, is able to overcome them, and they are under His control. ﴿And Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾; that is, Knowing of everything, Wise, placing things in their proper places. And from His knowledge and wisdom is that He legislated for you these sublime and beautiful rulings, and He has undertaken to suffice you regarding the matter of the captives and their evil should they intend betrayal.

This is a bond of loyalty and love that Allah established between the Emigrants (al-Muhajirun) who believed and emigrated in the way of Allah, leaving their homelands for Allah's sake, for the sake of striving (jihad) in the way of Allah, and the Helpers (al-Ansar) who sheltered the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions and aided them with their homes, their wealth and their persons. So these are allies of one another, because of the completeness of their faith and the perfect connection between them.

{And those who believed but did not emigrate, you have no obligation of protection toward them until they emigrate} For they severed the bond of protection with you by separating themselves from you at a time when there was great need for men. Since they did not emigrate, they had no share in the protection of the believers. Yet {if they seek your help in matters of religion}, that is, for the sake of fighting those who fight them, [for the sake of their religion], {then it is incumbent upon you to help them}, and to fight alongside them. As for those who fight them for other purposes, it is not incumbent upon you to help them. His saying, exalted is He: {except against a people between you and whom there is a covenant}, that is, a treaty to refrain from fighting; for when the believers who did not emigrate, and who are distinct from them, wish to fight them, do not assist them against those people, because of the covenant between you and them. {And Allah is Seeing of what you do}: He knows the states you are in, and so He legislates for you the rulings that are suitable for you.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 8, verse 73:

{73} When He established the bond of allegiance (wilayah) among the believers, He informed that the disbelievers, since disbelief brings them together, are allies of one another; so none will take them as allies except one who is a disbeliever like them. His words {unless you do it} mean: the allegiance of the believers and the enmity toward the disbelievers; by which is meant that you ally with them all, or you oppose them all, or you ally with the disbelievers and oppose the believers. {there will be fitnah (turmoil) on earth and great corruption}: for by that there will occur an immeasurable amount of evil, such as the mixing of truth with falsehood, of the believer with the disbeliever, and the loss of many great acts of worship such as jihad and hijrah (emigration), and other objectives of the Shari'ah and the religion which are lost when the believers are not taken, by themselves, as allies of one another.

The preceding verses concern the establishment of the bond of allegiance among the believers from the Muhajirun (Emigrants) and the Ansar (Helpers). And these verses explain their praise and their reward:

{74} He said: {And those who believed and emigrated and strove in the cause of Allah, and those who gave shelter and helped — those are the true believers}: meaning, of the Emigrants and the Helpers, they are {truly} the believers, because they confirmed their faith by what they did: the emigration (hijrah), the support, the loyalty of some of them to others, and their striving against their enemies among the disbelievers and the hypocrites. {For them is forgiveness}: from Allah, by which their misdeeds are erased and their slips are wiped away. {And} for them is {a generous provision}; that is, abundant good from the Generous Lord in the Gardens of Bliss, and it may be that they receive, in advance, some of the reward that comforts their eyes and sets their hearts at rest.

{75} And likewise, whoever came after these Emigrants and Helpers, of those who followed them in goodness, believed, emigrated and strove in the cause of Allah: {Those are of you}: they have what you have and they bear what you bear. This is the loyalty of faith, and it had a great effect and a great standing in the early days of Islam. The Prophet (ﷺ) established brotherhood between the Emigrants and the Helpers, a special brotherhood apart from the general brotherhood of faith, and to the extent that they would inherit from one another by it. Then Allah revealed: {And those related by blood are closer to one another in the Book of Allah}, so that a person's estate was inherited only by his blood relatives among the male agnatic heirs (ʻaṣabāt) and the sharers with fixed shares (aṣḥāb al-furūḍ); if there were none of these, then his nearest kin among the dhawu al-arḥām (distant blood relatives), as the generality of the noble verse indicates. His saying {in the Book of Allah} means: in His ruling and His legislation. {Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things}: and among that is what He knows of your conditions, and the religious laws that proceed from Him apply to you in accordance with them.

The commentary on Surah al-Anfal is complete. To Allah belongs all praise and grace.
